Use set_todos only when the request needs several steps or tool actions. Create the checklist before you start that work: give every item its required `active_form` (a present-participle phrase), mark the current item `in_progress` and the later items `pending`, and update the list as items finish, marking a finished item `completed`. A direct answer (a greeting, a question, a one-step reply) needs no checklist: answer it directly. Never call set_todos just to close a list right before your final reply; an item left `in_progress` at the end of the turn is fine. Pass `outcome` and the FULL `todos` list on every call; each call replaces the list, with no item IDs. Reuse the exact same `outcome` for the same unit of work. You have one active checklist in this session: changing `outcome` closes the previous checklist card as done and starts a new one. Your checklist is shown on the board and re-shown to you each turn. An `active_form` is required for every item: a short present-participle phrase such as "Drafting the Q4 summary", at most 500 characters, shown as the chat's working-on line while that item is `in_progress`. Use create_task with dependencies for a durable multi-wave plan, while tracking your own current work here.
